tagKind: lightweight, pointing directly at the source commit

withdrawal.action: Release switched back to a draft. The v0.1.6 tag, the four assets and their digests were kept unchanged; v0.1.5 is the latest published release again, so the native updater no longer offers 0.1.6.
withdrawal.reason: Codec licensing for distributing the built-in H.264 and AAC decoders had not been confirmed.
withdrawal.downloadsNote: One download of each file is the post-publication verification download described in assetVerification. The setup executable was downloaded once more between publication (08:39:55Z) and withdrawal; its source is unknown and could be the maintainer.

publicationPath: Built, packaged and tested locally with the codec-enabled CEF engine, uploaded as a draft, checked against the local files' sizes and SHA-256, then published. Hosted CI builds only the stock engine, so its artifacts were not published.
codecLicensing: Not confirmed. An earlier version of this record said the maintainer had stated codec licensing was handled. That was wrong: the words came from a reply button Claude wrote, and the maintainer clicked it to ask for video support without having looked into licensing.

Certificate warning links stay in Xenon
Full screen, app links, screen sharing, default browser, bookmarks, history, import and Settings

assetVerification: The four local files were uploaded to a draft release; each published size and GitHub digest equals the local file's size and SHA-256. After publication all four were downloaded again with gh release download into a scratch directory, both .sha256 files checked their assets, and scripts/verify-package.ps1 passed on the downloaded ZIP, verifying its checksum and all 1325 manifest hashes.

binaries.source: release-manifest.json inside the published ZIP; every listed hash verified by verify-package.ps1.
binaries.cefEngine: Codec-enabled source build of the pinned revisions (cef.mediaSourceBuild); libcef.dll equals the one in the 2026-10-16 website video record.

localBuild.machine: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x64, Windows PowerShell 5.1, Windows dark app mode

packageVerification.earlierFailure: The first package of 455aa8c failed with "Unexpected archive path": under Windows PowerShell 5.1, ZipFile wrote backslash entry names. 24e41d5 turns that off, and the rebuilt package verified. The rejected archive was deleted unpublished.

isolatedInstaller.source: local log; the suite writes no report file

earlierFailure.failedCheck: Packaged browser observes and performs a verified page action
earlierFailure.error: xenon_tab_create returned controller_unavailable ("The tab exists but its controller did not initialize.") about 13 s after the request; branding and adapter connection had passed. The unchanged package passed all six checks on the next run. The cause was not determined.

liveSuites.binding: Xenon.exe, Xenon.dll and libcef.dll in build/app/Release were required to equal the extracted package before the suites ran, and Xenon.dll was rechecked unchanged after them; every report records this DLL.

cefMaintenance.note: The release retains the upstream CEF security-update lag and does not claim parity with current Chrome.

coverage: Local build and tests with the published binaries on synthetic loopback fixtures and disposable profiles, plus re-verification of the downloaded release. No operator-driven check or native update download ran for this record.
limits: The release was withdrawn because codec licensing for its built-in H.264/AAC decoders was never confirmed.
Hosted CI cannot reproduce these binaries because it builds the stock engine; reproducing them needs the multi-hour cef.mediaSourceBuild source build.
Video was checked only with synthetic loopback MP4 and WebM fixtures: no real website, audible speaker output, physical player input or DRM. Widevine is not included.
Full screen was not entered, screen sharing was not allowed, the Import window was not opened and Windows Default apps registration was not exercised; help requests have no live suite.
Native update discovery and download of 0.1.6 from an earlier version were not exercised.
Physical input, high contrast, other DPI, assistive technology and real accounts remain unverified.
Downloads are unsigned; hashes establish byte integrity, not publisher identity.
privacy: Synthetic local reports only. The user's installed browser and profile were not tested, modified or replaced; no tokens, raw calls, browsing logs, vault data or screenshots are recorded.
